Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question during the Q&A session, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Mike Reynolds, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Mike Reynolds: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are John Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, VP of Exploration; and Brian Lee, VP of Marketing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to John Harlan.

John Harlan: Thank you, Mike, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes averaging 525,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 12% year-over-year. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on exploration and drilling activities, where standout well results in the Permian and Eagle Ford underscore our technical edge. We are focused on future development plans that leverage our vast resource potential across Tier 1 basins. Further, we added significant proved reserves this year, achieving an organic reserve replacement ratio of 115%. We continue to adjust to market dynamics through prudent hedging and cost discipline. Finally, we are taking steps to optimize our debt profile, reducing net debt meaningfully while maintaining investment-grade leverage.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, John. As John mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $3.9 billion, up 22% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.8 billion, and net income was $1.3 billion. We generated $1.2 billion in free cash flow and returned $800 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $14.8 billion in total debt and $3.5 billion in cash.

Let me turn to our adjusted EBITDA, which came in at $2.45 billion for the quarter, representing a robust 28% year-over-year increase from $1.91 billion in Q3 2023. On a trailing twelve-month basis, EBITDA now stands at $9.8 billion, up 22% year-over-year, underscoring the strength of our integrated upstream portfolio amid a resilient commodity environment. Let me break down the key drivers behind this outperformance, starting with the top line and then drilling into our operational leverage.

First, realized pricing was a primary tailwind. Our blended realized oil price averaged $78.50 per barrel, up 18% from $66.40 in the prior-year quarter, driven by firmer Brent benchmarks averaging $84 per barrel—bolstered by ongoing OPEC+ production cuts and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Natural gas realizations held steady at $3.25 per Mcf, benefiting from robust LNG demand in Europe, while NGLs fetched $28 per barrel amid strong petrochemical margins. Importantly, our hedging program mitigated downside risk, with 65% of our oil volumes hedged at a floor of $75 per barrel through year-end, shielding us from intra-quarter WTI volatility that dipped below $75 at times.

Production volumes grew 12% year-over-year to a record 525,000 boe per day, with oil comprising 68% of the mix. This was led by our Permian Basin assets, where net production ramped to 220,000 boe/d—up 25% year-over-year—thanks to the full-year contribution from our $1.2 billion Bolt-on acquisition in the Delaware Basin last December, which added 40,000 boe/d of high-margin inventory. In the Eagle Ford, we hit 110,000 boe/d, a 15% increase, fueled by longer laterals averaging 12,000 feet and enhanced completions with our proprietary 'ApexPro' diverter technology, which improved stage-level EURs by 18% in our recent 15-well pad. Offshore, Guyana's Stabroek Block—where we hold a 20% stake alongside ExxonMobil and Hess—delivered first oil from the Yellowtail project ahead of schedule, contributing 25,000 boe/d at $4 netback per boe after royalties.

Regionally, North America drove 70% of the volume growth, with our U.S. onshore operations achieving a 92% operating efficiency despite weather disruptions in the Bakken. Internationally, Brazil's pre-salt Campos Basin ramped to 60,000 boe/d post-FPUs on our Buzios Phase 3 development, capitalizing on Petrobras' aggressive local content waivers. However, we saw some offset in the North Sea, where UK Brent production dipped 5% to 35,000 boe/d due to field maturation and higher cyclone downtime, though our Rosebank tie-back initiative positions us for 50,000 boe/d gross by 2026.

Shifting to the bottom line, our cost discipline amplified these topline gains, delivering $12.50 per boe in cash operating costs—down 8% year-over-year from $13.60. Lease operating expenses fell to $6.80 per boe through automated pump-off controls and our enterprise-wide digital twin platform, which reduced unplanned downtime by 22% across 1,200 wells. Gathering and transportation costs improved 10% to $3.20 per boe, aided by our midstream JV with Enterprise Products Partners, optimizing NGL fractionation at our Mont Belvieu hub. DD&A held flat at $18 per boe, reflecting efficient reserve replacement at a 140% ratio, with 95% proved developed producing.

Strategic initiatives also played a pivotal role. We realized $150 million in synergies from the Bolt-on deal—15% ahead of plan—through shared services and centralized drilling rigs, dropping Permian breakevens to $42 per barrel WTI. Our $800 million share repurchase under the expanded program, funded by free cash flow yield of 18%, further enhanced shareholder returns. Looking ahead, we're allocating 55% of our $4.2 billion 2024 capex to high-return Permian inventory, with four-rig program targeting 15% growth, while advancing carbon capture pilots in the Eagle Ford to capture Section 45Q credits.

In summary, this 28% EBITDA growth reflects the resilience of our Tier 1 assets, prudent hedging, and relentless focus on capital efficiency in a $80-plus oil world. Compared to peers, our margins of 62% outpace ExxonMobil's 58% and Chevron's 55%, positioning us for sustained multi-year cash flow generation.

Before moving on, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our debt profile, net debt position, and leverage metrics. Our disciplined capital allocation has continued to deliver meaningful deleveraging amid a volatile macro environment, with WTI averaging $78 per barrel and Brent at $82 through the quarter—pressured by OPEC+ production decisions and softening Chinese demand, but supported by robust U.S. LNG exports.

As of September 30th, our total debt stood at $14.8 billion, comprising $12.5 billion in long-term unsecured notes and term loans, $1.2 billion in short-term revolver draws, and $1.1 billion in finance leases primarily tied to our offshore FPSO assets in the North Sea. This represents a 5% quarter-over-quarter reduction from $15.6 billion at Q2 end, driven by $850 million in scheduled maturities—mainly the repayment of our 2021 vintage 4.75% senior notes—and $450 million in opportunistic buybacks at a discount to par. Year-to-date, we've shaved total debt by 12% from $16.8 billion at year-end 2023, reflecting our commitment to front-loading repayments using excess free cash flow generation.

Our weighted average cost of debt remains attractive at 4.6%, down 20 basis points from last quarter following the refinancing of $2 billion in 2024 maturities into a new five-year term loan at SOFR plus 175 bps. This locks in sub-5% blended rates ahead of potential Fed cuts, shielding us from near-term interest rate volatility. Notably, 65% of our debt is fixed-rate, with an average maturity of 4.8 years, providing stability as we navigate the contango in the forward curve out to 2026.

We ended the quarter with $2.4 billion in cash and cash equivalents, plus $1.1 billion in marketable securities—bolstered by $1.2 billion in restricted cash from our Permian joint ventures with ExxonMobil and Chevron. This brings net debt to $11.3 billion, a $1.1 billion improvement sequentially and 18% lower year-over-year. Excluding the $800 million in JV cash that's contractually ring-fenced for Angola block development, our core net debt is even stronger at $10.5 billion. This positions us flexibly for seasonal working capital needs and potential M&A opportunities in high-quality Tier 1 acreage.

On leverage ratios, our headline metric—net debt to TTM Adjusted EBITDA—improved to 2.7x from 3.1x at Q2 and 3.9x at year-end 2023. This is well within our target range of 1.0x to 2.5x, and compares favorably to peers like ConocoPhillips at 2.4x and EOG Resources at 1.8x. Credit-adjusted, factoring in our $3.2 billion undrawn revolver capacity, we're at an effective 1.9x—investment-grade territory. Debt-to-capitalization sits at 28%, down from 32% last year.

Regionally, our U.S. onshore portfolio drives strong debt servicing capacity. We're prioritizing asset monetization, enhanced hedging, and RCF optimization to sustain this trajectory. We're on track for 2.0x leverage by Q4 2025, supporting dividend growth and share repurchases.

Finally on financials, before we open it up to questions, I'd like to dive deep into our proved reserves additions, with a particular focus on our reserve replacement ratio—or RRR—and the organic growth that's fueling our long-term value creation. For full-year 2024 to date, we added 142 million barrels of oil equivalent—or MMboe—of proved reserves under SEC guidelines. This brings our year-end total proved reserves to a record 1.8 billion BOE, up 9% from prior year. Against production, this translates to an all-in reserve replacement ratio of 120%. Even more impressively, our organic reserve replacement ratio, excluding any acquisitions or divestitures, came in at 115%. That's the fifth straight year we've delivered organic RRR north of 100%, outpacing peers.

Our additions were driven by 45% from successful exploration and appraisal drilling, 32% from positive revisions and extensions, 18% from improved field performance via enhanced recovery techniques. Finding and development costs remained disciplined at $12.50 per BOE, down 8%. In the Permian Basin, accounting for 55% of additions, we replaced 135% organically through Delaware Basin stack plays and cube development. Eagle Ford added strong volumes with infill programs. Internationally, Gulf of Mexico and Namibia contributed meaningfully.

On the technical front, next-gen seismic and CCUS pilots have engineered this growth. Strategically, this supports our drill-bit growth mantra, with 110-120% organic RRR projected for full-year.

I will now turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez for an operational update.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Alex. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 525,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Bone Spring Pad 7 online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

To provide more granularity on production volumes, which continue to underscore our disciplined execution. In Q3, we averaged 158,000 BOE/d total production in our core U.S. onshore assets, up 4% quarter-over-quarter from 152,000 BOE/d in Q2, and 9% year-over-year from 145,000 BOE/d in Q3 2023. Oil volumes hit 98,000 bbl/d, 62% of mix, up 7% QoQ and 15% YoY, reflecting Delaware Basin pads with ApexFlow completions. Gas volumes stable at 360 MMcf/d or 60,000 BOE/d. Permian led at 134,000 BOE/d, up 6% QoQ. Q4 guidance 160-165,000 BOE/d, positioning for 5-7% growth in 2025.

Now, I'd like to turn to our exploration and drilling updates, where we've continued to execute with discipline amid a supportive commodity backdrop—WTI holding steady around $82 per barrel and Henry Hub natural gas at $3.40 per MMBtu. In the Permian Basin, our core Delaware Basin position—spanning over 150,000 net acres—saw 18 horizontal wells online across three pads in the Second Bone Spring and Wolfcamp A/B. Average 24-hour IP of 1,450 boe/d, 65% oil, 60-day at 950 boe/d. Bone Spring Pad 7 with 12,500-foot laterals and Vanguard Completion Design delivered 1,950 boe/d IP, 1.8 MMboe EUR, 15% uplift. Success rate 100%, drill times 18 days.

In Eagle Ford, six new wells averaged 1,100 boe/d IP, Maverick Pad highlight with 14,000-foot laterals boosting EURs 20%. Internationally, Beacon-2 in Gulf of Mexico confirmed 150 feet net pay, 120 MMboe resource. Namibia Orange Basin prospect 500 MMboe.

Technical initiatives like FracAI reduced cycle times 12%, electric frack fleets cut emissions 40%. Future plans: $650M H2 D&C, four Permian rigs, two Eagle Ford, targeting 85 gross wells. Inventory 850 locations, 60% Tier 1. This positions us for 8-10% PDP growth.

Now I will turn it over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for an update on our exploration activities.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Maria. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and Gulf of Mexico and are planning to drill 55 net exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio, building on our 115% organic RRR and high-impact prospects like Namibia's Block 4. Our focus remains on de-risking contingent resources through advanced analytics and strategic partnerships.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Brian Lee to discuss our marketing strategy.

Brian Lee: Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for NGLs in the Mont Belvieu market area, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of these petrochemical-linked realizations is significant, supporting our margins amid LNG export growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. At this time, to ask a question, please press star then 1. Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning, team. Strong quarter—congrats on the beat. I wanted to dive into your future development plans and resource potential. With WTI holding around $82 per barrel and Brent at $86, how are you prioritizing your inventory amid the consolidation wave? Any updates on the Permian stack pay potential or Guyana analogs?

John Harlan: Thanks, Sarah, and good morning everyone. Great question, and we're excited about the runway ahead. I'll walk through our future development plans and resource potential in detail. As you know, at Apex Energy Corp., our strategy remains laser-focused on high-return, oil-weighted inventory in Tier 1 basins, leveraging our technical edge to unlock multi-zone potential while advancing our net-zero ambitions by 2050.

Let me start with the big picture on our resource base. As of year-end 2024, our proved developed producing reserves—or PDP—stand at 1.2 billion barrels of oil equivalent, or BOE, with total proved reserves at 2.1 billion BOE. Drilling down to 2P reserves, we're at 4.8 billion BOE, up 12% year-over-year, driven by successful delineation in the Permian and our Bakken core. On the 3P side, contingent resources add another 7.2 billion BOE unrisked. This gives us a robust 15-year drilling inventory at current paces, with over 4,000 gross locations identified across our portfolio—more than 70% Tier 1.

Regionally, the Permian remains our crown jewel, accounting for 65% of our 2025 capex at $1.8 billion. We've got 2,500 undrilled locations in the Delaware Basin alone, targeting the stacked pay from the Second Bone Spring through the Wolfcamp benches. Recent results show Q4 Wolfcamp C laterals averaging 1,400 BOE per day over 30 days, with 65% oil cut. We're accelerating with 12 rigs in Q1 2025, aiming for 10-12% production growth to 450,000 BOE per day by year-end. Long-term, our internal models project 20% EUR uplift on 30% of inventory.

Shifting to the Bakken, 25% of capex at $700 million, we've derisked 800 locations, Q4 IP-30 rates 1,800 BOE per day. Internationally, Gulf of Mexico Salina Bay starts first oil H2 2026, net 15,000 BOE/d. Namibia Mopane-1X spuds Q2 2025, targeting 1.5 billion unrisked barrels.

On technical initiatives, AI-driven mapping identified 15% more Tier 1 acreage, electrified fracs cut emissions 25% YoY, Permian CCUS hub targets 5 million tonnes CO2 by 2030. Capex guiding $2.8-3.2 billion for 2025, targeting 8-10% annual growth through 2027. Amid OPEC+ cuts, we're positioned for consolidation with $500 million dry powder.

Mike, anything to add?

Mike Reynolds: Spot on, John. Sarah, to quantify resource potential: we've booked 450 million BOE of 2024 extensions and discoveries, replacing 125% of production. Full details in our 10-K supplement.

John Harlan: Exactly. Forward-looking statements apply—actual results may differ due to commodity prices, regs, etc.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. What are your expectations for debt levels and leverage ratios going forward?

Alex Rivera: Good morning, John. As I detailed earlier, we're on a clear deleveraging path to 2.0x net debt/EBITDA by year-end 2025, supported by free cash flow and asset sales. Our fixed-rate structure and hedging provide resilience.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Torres with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Torres: Could you please provide more color on production volumes and changes?

Maria Gonzalez: Thanks, Lisa. Good morning. As outlined, our Q3 volumes showed solid QoQ and YoY gains driven by Permian ramps, with Q4 guidance firm and 2025 uplift from efficient D&C.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Reilly with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Reilly: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Mark. Our exploration successes, like Beacon-2 and Namibia prospects, directly bolster our 15-year inventory, shifting capex toward high-IRR developments while maintaining 15% exploration allocation for upside.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Wong: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years?

Brian Lee: Good morning, David. Our NGL marketing in Mont Belvieu remains strong, with outlook bright on petrochemical demand and LNG growth. We're expanding contracts for multi-year uplift.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to John Harlan for closing remarks.

John Harlan: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
